items.front: DPSP — Part, Articles and borrowed from?
items.back: Part IV, Articles 36-51; borrowed from the Irish Constitution (which took it from Spain).
items.examPoint: Part IV, Articles 36-51 — placement & scope of DPSP

items.front: What does Article 37 say about DPSP?
items.back: Non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts) yet 'fundamental in the governance of the country'; State's duty to apply them.
items.examPoint: Article 37 — not enforceable yet fundamental in governance; duty of State to apply

items.front: Which part of the Constitution declares the ideal of a Welfare State?
items.back: The Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV).
items.examPoint: Objective — welfare state; social, economic & political justice; economic democracy

items.back: Material resources serve the common good; wealth and means of production are not concentrated to common detriment.
items.examPoint: Article 39 — livelihood, wealth distribution, equal pay for equal work

items.front: Separation of the judiciary from the executive is enjoined by which DPSP?
items.examPoint: Article 50 — separation of judiciary from executive

items.front: Promotion of international peace and security is which Article?
items.examPoint: Article 48A & Article 51 — environment protection; international peace

items.front: Which DPSP did the 42nd Amendment (1976) add?
items.back: Art 39A (free legal aid), Art 43A (workers' participation in management), Art 48A (environment).

items.front: Article 43B (added by which amendment) covers what?
items.back: Promotion of cooperative societies; added by the 97th Amendment, 2011.

items.front: Where is 'economic justice' provided as an objective?
items.back: In the Preamble AND the Directive Principles of State Policy.
items.examPoint: Objective — welfare state; social, economic & political justice; economic democracy

items.front: Are DPSP limitations on the legislative/executive functions of the State?
items.back: No — they are positive directions (goals) for State action, not limitations on its powers.
items.examPoint: Non-justiciable nature — not enforceable by courts

items.front: FR vs DPSP — the case line ending in the current balance?
items.back: Champakam (1951 FR prevail) → Golaknath (1967) → Kesavananda (1973)/Minerva Mills (1980): balance is basic structure. Art 31C shields 39(b)/(c).
items.examPoint: Kesavananda Bharati (1973) & Minerva Mills (1980) — FR-DPSP balance; Article 31C

items.front: Article 44 vs Article 40 — which is which?
items.back: Art 44 = Uniform Civil Code (Liberal); Art 40 = organisation of village panchayats (Gandhian).
